title: What does XLS-38 specify for Cross-chain bridges?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-38 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-38 specifies witness-based cross-chain bridges connecting designated door accounts. [1]

Transfers involve a source commitment, witness attestations and destination-side claims. The bridge configuration binds assets and chains; it does not make any two tokens automatically equivalent. Account-creation transfers have their own attestation path. Security depends on the selected witness arrangement and both networks, so source-chain inclusion alone is insufficient evidence of completed delivery. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-38 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-38 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
